core_obligations: Translate the first condition: for distinct closed points x and y, the union of x and y as a closed subscheme is zero dimensional of degree two, and surjectivity for it gives a section vanishing at one and not the other (proof lines 4401-4403).

Translate the second condition: a nonzero tangent vector at a closed point defines a morphism from the spectrum of the dual numbers which is a closed immersion, and its image is a zero dimensional closed subscheme of degree two, so surjectivity for that subscheme supplies a section vanishing at the point with nonvanishing pullback along the vector (proof lines 4404-4407).
Apply the separation lemma to conclude very ampleness (proof lines 4398-4400).
proof_roadmap: Sufficiency of the hypotheses of the separation lemma (proof lines 4399-4400).
difficulty_reason: Over an algebraically closed field k, for a proper k-scheme X with an invertible sheaf L, the lemma concludes that L is very ample provided the restriction map on global sections surjects onto the sections of L over every zero dimensional closed subscheme of degree two (statement lines 4385-4396). The proof is a reformulation: given two distinct closed points, their union viewed as a closed subscheme of degree two gives the first hypothesis of the separation lemma, and given a nonzero tangent vector, the associated morphism from the spectrum of the dual numbers is a closed immersion whose image is a zero dimensional subscheme of degree two giving the second hypothesis (proof lines 4398-4407). The separation lemma then yields very ampleness. The claim is H2: a clean translation between two formulations, with the identification of the image of a tangent vector as a degree two subscheme as the only step needing care.
